blocks.x: Case selection on a governed risk spine, audit yield up 12% and taxpayer touchpoints down 35% through better targeting
Identity withheld, a national tax authority whose audit selection was a weighted lottery and whose compliance teams knew it. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline year measured the lottery: audit yield 31% below the internal target, selection rules opaque even to their owners, and legitimate taxpayers pulled into audits because the rules couldn't tell effort from evasion.
Data existed across registries, filings and third-party reports but never joined. The selection rulebook had accreted for fifteen years, and no one could say which rules still earned their keep.

We rebuilt selection on a governed risk spine: registries and filings resolved to one taxpayer model with lineage auditors can walk, risk signals evaluated against closed-case outcomes so rules are scored not assumed, case selection ranked with reasons attached for every file, and the rulebook versioned under a governance board with retired rules documented. The lottery became targeting; the targeting became defensible.
